answer: A slashable stake bond is a concrete Sybil defense. Before an agent may vote or earn, it must lock collateral; identity is then priced in that deposit, not in cheaply minted keys. A thousand fake accounts need a thousand bonds, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every impersonation. Random audits slash the full bond of any node caught double-voting, so fraud burns a bright ember of its own capital. Think of a guarded wharf: every berth is bonded, and whether a ship carries yarrow or iron it pays the same fee to dock, so Sybil forgery costs real savings.
